transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-03 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE); Priya Desai (Redwood SE); Sam Huang (Redwood CSM); Marta Gomez (Acme Head of ML); Ethan Cole (Acme Infra); Lena Park (Acme Security); Nikhil Rao (Acme Product)

Summary: Quick signoff on success criteria for POC, agree benchmark plan, assign owners and due dates, schedule benchmark window.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I think we have most of the decision makers on. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Marta Gomez: Marta here.
[00:14] Ethan Cole: Ethan.
[00:16] Lena Park: Lena.
[00:18] Nikhil Rao: Nikhil.
[00:20] Priya Desai: Priya from Redwood SE.
[00:22] Jordan Lee: Great. Goal today is to lock down the success criteria and benchmark plan for the POC so we can run the baseline next week.

[02:05] Marta: To frame it — our production use is a customer-facing summarization and routing flow. Peak QPS is around 25 requests per second, average payload 1.2k tokens, peaks up to 3k. Latency is very important for UX, but cost also matters.

[03:10] Priya: That helps. For scoping we typically look at p50/p95 latency, tokens per second, and cost per 1k tokens after batching. For quality we'll want a semantic accuracy check — can you confirm the eval methodology?

[03:55] Marta: We'll use a 500-sample golden set with human labels for correctness and coherence. Our internal bar is ~90% pass rate on the golden set for the initial POC.

[05:20] Jordan: Ok so tentatively quality pass >= 90% on 500 samples. For latency thresholds — what's your go/no-go?

[05:45] Ethan: Ideally p95 < 250ms, but if we move to hosted initial pilot we can accept up to 350ms. Cost target we'd like to see <$0.003 per token on average after batching.

[06:30] Priya: Helpful. Cognizant that tokens/word estimates vary, we'll run both single-request latency and batched throughput to show tradeoffs. We'll provide a benchmarking spreadsheet and dashboard CSV.

[07:40] Nikhil: How do you handle fallbacks and routing? If the model is overloaded, we need predictable degradation.

[08:15] Priya: Redwood has smart routing and automatic fallback to smaller model variants; for POC we'll configure a canary route and explicit fallback policy. We'll include that in the runbook.

[10:02] Lena: Security: we need SOC 2, SSO/SAML, and an HSM/KMS integration for keys in Private deployment. For the hosted POC, we need a statement of data retention, encryption at rest/in transit, and audit logs.

[10:40] Jordan: We'll share our SOC 2 and security pack. For the POC we can run on hosted — no customer data will be stored, and keys can be customer-managed if you prefer.

[12:55] Marta: Good. Another question — are you planning to run baseline on Redwood hosted then a dedicated run if numbers improve?

[13:20] Priya: Yes, recommended path: baseline on hosted (fast to get data), then optional dedicated run with pinned capacity if you need lower p95 and isolation. We'll cost both options.

[15:00] Ethan: For dedicated, what are typical node counts for 25 QPS with average 1.2k token requests?

[15:22] Priya: Rough estimate — with aggressive batching you can often get to 25 QPS on 2-3 A100-class GPUs for generation workloads depending on model size. We'll provide a modeling sheet with tokenization and KV cache characteristics.

[17:10] Jordan: Let's lock the measurable acceptance tests:
- Quality: >=90% semantic pass on 500-sample golden set
- Latency (hosted baseline): p95 <= 350ms; p50 <= 120ms
- Latency (dedicated target if run): p95 <= 250ms
- Cost: mean token cost <= $0.003 per token after batching and caching (report both raw and optimized)
- Throughput: sustain 25 QPS for 10 minutes without error rate >1%

[19:05] Marta: Those look reasonable. We might relax p95 to 400ms if quality is significantly better, but prefer 350 as target.

[20:30] Priya: For reporting format we'll produce: a CSV with request-level latencies and token counts, a summary dashboard with p50/p95/p99, cost breakdown per model & per 1k tokens, and a quality report with sample failures. We'll also provide an evaluation harness script that you can run locally to reproduce numbers.

[22:12] Nikhil: How will you measure semantic pass? Is that automated or manual?

[22:28] Priya: The golden set will be human-labeled; we'll run model outputs through an automated rubric for initial scoring and sample manual review for edge cases. We'll provide the scoring script.

[24:00] Ethan: Network — we might want to test VPC peering for dedicated. For hosted we need to know allowed IP ranges and outbound egress rules.

[24:30] Jordan: We'll share network requirements and options. For hosted POC no peering required, but we'll list IP ranges and allow-list entries.

[26:00] Marta: Timeline? We want baseline results within two weeks.

[26:20] Jordan: Proposed timeline:
- 11/05: Redwood sends POC plan + security pack + pricing
- 11/06: Acme delivers sample workload and infra constraints
- Week of 11/10: Run hosted baseline and report by end of that week
- Optional dedicated run week of 11/17 if needed

[28:40] Marta: Sounds good. One other procurement note — we need a short SOW and a month-to-month POC contract.

[29:05] Sam Huang: We can provide a template SOW for pilots, Jordan will share contract language.

[31:10] Priya: On benchmarks: we'll run three phases — cold start single-request latencies, steady-state batched throughput, and a 10-minute sustain test at 25 QPS. We'll capture token-level metrics and cost.

[33:55] Ethan: Can you include KV cache behavior in the report? We have variable session lengths and reuse of context.

[34:20] Priya: Yes, we'll include KV cache hit rates and show improvements from prefix caching. We'll also show model quantization options and estimated CPU/GPU utilization.

[36:50] Lena: For security signoff after the POC we will need audit logs and proof of key handling. If you do dedicated we will want KMS integration with our cloud provider.

[37:30] Jordan: Noted. We'll include the KMS/HSM integration options in the security pack.

[39:00] Marta: If the hosted numbers meet acceptance criteria we'll move to a 3-month pilot with reserved capacity.

[40:10] Jordan: Perfect. Let's read back the acceptance tests and next steps to confirm.

[40:25] Priya: Acceptance tests: quality >=90% on 500-sample gold set; hosted p95 <=350ms; dedicated p95 <=250ms if executed; cost <= $0.003/token (mean after batching); sustain 25 QPS for 10 minutes without >1% error rate.

[41:00] Marta: Acceptable. We approve, subject to seeing the actual benchmark CSV and the security pack.

[42:20] Jordan: Next steps recap: Jordan to send POC plan, security docs, and pricing by 11/05. Acme to send sample workload and infra constraints by 11/06. Priya to run hosted baseline and deliver CSV + dashboard by 11/14.

[43:35] Nikhil: Are we documenting what constitutes a "pass" for quality ties? Like if quality is 88% but latency is 200ms do we move forward?

[44:00] Marta: We'll evaluate holistically — Jordan, include a note in the SOW about escalation to product owners if thresholds fall in a gray area.

[45:20] Priya: We'll also include an examples appendix — representative success and failure cases — to make the quality discussion concrete.

[46:55] Ethan: Anything else on reporting format? CSV columns we need: request_id, timestamp, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, kv_cache_hit, error_code.

[47:20] Priya: We'll use that as the baseline CSV schema and include a sample.

[49:00] Jordan: Okay to send the calendar invite for the benchmark run?

[49:10] Marta: Yes, week of 11/10 works.

[50:00] Jordan: Great. Quick closing: everyone aligned?
[50:12] Marta: Aligned.
[50:15] Lena: Aligned pending security doc review.
[50:20] Ethan: Aligned.
[50:30] Nikhil: Aligned.

[52:00] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the plan and action items.
[54:30] (call ends)

References/attachments mentioned: POC runbook (will be shared), security pack (SOC 2 + KMS options), benchmarking spreadsheet (CSV + dashboard link).

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription with occasional name/Acronym errors (e.g., KV cache transcribed as "K V cash" in one pass) — manual cleanup applied to key items.
